chunks: And ʿUmar ibn Yazīd narrated from him that he said:

None of you performs an obligatory prayer in its time, then performs prayer with them as taqiyyah while he is in a state of wudu (ablution), except that Allah records for him thereby twenty-five درجات of reward. So desire that.

key_terms.تَقِيَّةً: precautionary dissimulation for protection in a sensitive setting
key_terms.خَمْسًا وَ عِشْرِينَ دَرَجَةً: twenty-five درجات of reward or rank
key_terms.فَارْغَبُوا: so seek eagerly or be desirous of
key_terms.فَرِيضَةً: an obligatory prayer prescribed by Allah
key_terms.مُتَوَضِّئٌ: being in a state of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying with others out of taqiyyah after already performing the obligatory prayer on time?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages one who has already performed the obligatory salat in its proper time to join others in prayer when required by taqiyyah, provided he remains in a state of wudu (ablution). It states that such participation brings a reward of twenty-five degrees, showing the merit of preserving both proper worship and prudent communal conduct.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1124 - It is narrated from him by Umar ibn Yazid that Imam (as) said:

"None of you prays an obligatory prayer at its prescribed time and then prays with them (in congregation) as an act of precaution (taqiyya) while in a state of wudu, except that Allah (swt) will record for him twenty-five degrees (of reward). So strive for this."
